component.name: Repeat That
component.summary: Replay what was just said on a call

description.p: Missed what someone just said on a call? Press a key and hear it again. Repeat That keeps a short rolling buffer of the audio from one app you pick, such as Discord, Teams, Zoom or your browser, leaves out the silence, and replays the last thing that was said whenever you press a hotkey.

ul.li: Replays the last sentence, and steps back one more with each extra press
Catch-up speeds the replay up from where it is and stops when it reaches live
Lowers the app's volume while it replays, so you hear the replay
Global hotkeys on X11, and through the GlobalShortcuts portal on KDE Plasma and GNOME 48 or later

description.p: The audio stays in memory and is never written to disk. Nothing is uploaded, there is no telemetry and no account, and only the app you pick is captured, never your microphone.

In this Flatpak, Repeat That reaches PipeWire through its socket, which it needs to list the apps that play sound, capture the one you pick and lower its volume. It needs PipeWire with WirePlumber, which current desktops use by default.
